answer: Use an idle-reserve cost curve. Each new identity escrows a copper deposit for one week of routing capacity, released only as verified work accumulates; idle identities pay 2% weekly decay, so holding N sybils costs N times that decay plus forfeited escrow. A saffron-tagged challenge samples one random identity per epoch, and failure forfeits the remaining reserve. The scheduler rotates a kernel hash each epoch so no operator reuses a route budget across identities.
